chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'A boy who had stolen was brought to Ali (peace be upon him). He scratched his fingers, then said:
Indeed, if you were to repeat (the theft), I would cut them.
Then he said: 'But it has not been done except by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and myself.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) say about cutting fingers for theft?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the unique judicial authority of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in applying the hadd penalty for theft, specifically noting that the cutting of fingers was a practice exclusive to the Prophet and the Imam. It underscores the continuity of prophetic legal tradition within Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam acts as the direct successor in implementing divine penalties. The narration serves to validate the authenticity of the theft penalty as derived directly from the Prophet's practice.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from his companion, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a boy who had stolen. So he<sup>asws</sup> scratched his fingers, then said: ‘But, if you were to repeat, I would cut these’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But it has not been done except by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and myself<sup>asws</sup>’.
